$comment: COPY → ~/.paseo-pi-team/pi-models.local.json on each host that routes to pi. Never commit the local copy: it names host-specific endpoints. `pteam models sync` reads this, probes every model each endpoint lists, and rewrites ONE entry per provider in ~/.pi/agent/models.json — providers absent from this file are left alone. Each key under 'providers' is the pi provider name, so a route's model reads '<provider-name>/<model-id>'; it must not contain a slash, because Paseo splits that reference at the FIRST slash only. Add as many endpoints as you like: they are written in one pass, and one whose endpoint is down keeps the models it already had instead of losing them. The API key is NEVER stored here — 'keyEnv' names the environment variable pi resolves at runtime, and 'keyFile' is where `pteam models sync` looks when that variable is unset; point it at the same file systemd hands the daemon via EnvironmentFile= so the secret lives in exactly one place. 'probe: false' writes whatever the endpoint lists without checking it answers, which is only safe on an endpoint that never lists a dead model. Each model's contextWindow/maxTokens come from models.dev (https://models.dev/api.json, cached for a day under the team directory's cache/, a stale copy used when offline) when its id matches there unambiguously; otherwise they are left out of models.json, which means unknown. 'models' is optional and holds per-model overrides keyed by the id the endpoint lists — use it for an id models.dev does not know (a proxy alias, a '-free' variant) or when the endpoint caps lower than the upstream model. A model may also carry 'compat': pi compat flags written verbatim and merged over what pi auto-detects from the baseUrl — the case that earns it is a reasoning model behind a generic OpenAI proxy whose backend rejects the 'developer' role with a 422, fixed by {"supportsDeveloperRole": false}. There is no endpoint-wide contextWindow/maxTokens: older files that still have one are ignored with a warning.
